messages:
Ibrahim Khan: Kicking off a decision we need for the parity spec: retries *default on* vs *opt-in*. We keep getting support issues where one SDK retries and another doesn’t, but SRE has been (rightly) nervous about retry storms. Want opinions + SRE guidance. Context: SUP-9334 (TS retries too aggressively on 429) + a bunch of 5xx flaps last week.

Dana Lo: +1 we need a default. But “default on” can backfire in Node bc people run high concurrency and then `fetch` retries amplify. If we do default, it has to be conservative and respect `Retry-After` and rate-limit headers.

Mateusz Zielinski: Go users lean on context deadlines; retries w/ no budget will bite. I’m fine with default-on if we have a strict retry budget + clear classification. Otherwise opt-in.

Monica Patel: From support side, “no retries by default” means every enterprise customer re-implements it slightly differently and then blames us when they get thundering herd. But “aggressive retries by default” also becomes a support nightmare. Need SRE to give us safe guardrails.

Rafael Mendes: looping in. Biggest risks:
1) retry storms on 429 if you don’t honor `Retry-After` / reset headers
2) synchronized backoff (no jitter)
3) unlimited retries + no overall cap -> queue buildup + longer tail latency
If default-on, must include: max attempts cap, exponential backoff w/ full jitter, and a *retry budget* (limit total time spent retrying). Also: do NOT retry non-idempotent requests unless we can guarantee idempotency.

Tomáš Novák: +1. Also watch out for “fast retries” on connection errors. A lot of transient dial resets in customer VPCs; without jitter they all retry instantly. It’s the classic amplification.

Ethan Park: From gateway side, 429 semantics: we return `Retry-After` today in most places, but it’s not 100% consistent across all routes yet. There’s a platform PR in flight to make it consistent. But we should assume: if `Retry-After` exists, honor it; if not, use backoff.

Amara Diallo: For rate limits specifically, we have `x-ratelimit-limit`, `x-ratelimit-remaining`, `x-ratelimit-reset` for some endpoints. Payload also has an error code. But I agree: SDK should not depend on those always existing.

Brian Murphy: API ergonomics angle: customers *expect* basic retries for “obviously transient” failures (network, 503, 502). But we need a clean escape hatch and predictable defaults. I’d avoid a world where TS defaults differ from Python.

Dana Lo: What’s “conservative default” numerically? Right now TS PR prototype was 5 attempts for 429/5xx which is too much. We should probably be like 2-3 tries max?

Rafael Mendes: My recommendation for default:
- retryable: 408, 409 (maybe), 429, 500, 502, 503, 504 + transport errors (DNS, connect reset, TLS handshake) where safe
- max attempts: 3 total (1 initial + 2 retries)
- backoff: exponential starting at 200ms, cap ~2s, full jitter
- retry budget: cap total retry time at ~10s for non-streaming calls
- always respect `Retry-After` when present (but cap to something reasonable like 30s unless caller opts-in)
Also: detect/avoid retrying when caller timeout is already near-expired.

Mateusz Zielinski: For Go we can implement that cleanly w/ context + deadlines. We can also expose `RetryOptions{MaxAttempts, MaxElapsedTime}`.

Ibrahim Khan: Question on 409 — do we actually have semantics that make it safe? Or do we risk retrying a conflict that’s logical not transient?

Brian Murphy: I’d be cautious. 409 in our API isn’t really used for transient conflicts; it’s usually “state mismatch”. Suggest: no 409 in default classifier.

Amara Diallo: Agree. 409 isn’t a common transient on gateway for us.

Dana Lo: Another edge: POST /chat.completions isn’t idempotent from a billing perspective if the request hits and client times out on response. If SDK retries automatically, customer might pay twice.

Rafael Mendes: Exactly. This is where idempotency keys matter. Without an idempotency mechanism, default retries should avoid retrying after the request is fully sent if we can’t know whether server processed it.

Ethan Park: We do have `request-id` in responses; we don’t have an idempotency key header for chat completions today (we’ve discussed it). So SDK needs to be careful. Transport errors before write are safer; after write/response-start is ambiguous.

Tomáš Novák: One suggestion: treat “connect errors / TLS handshake / DNS” as safe to retry. Treat “read timeout / socket hang up after bytes sent” as maybe-not unless idempotency is present. Many SDKs don’t distinguish perfectly though.

Nadia Rahman: From client instrumentation: if we do retries, we should emit hooks/metrics so we can detect retry amplification (attempt count, reason, backoff, total elapsed). Otherwise SRE only sees it indirectly at gateway.

Monica Patel: +1, and support needs request IDs surfaced. When customers paste logs, we need correlation.

Dana Lo: For TS, Node `undici` vs `fetch` errors differ. But we can normalize error types to “connect vs read vs timeout”. We’ll need a classifier table and tests.

Mateusz Zielinski: Go can reliably tell `net.Error` timeout, context cancellation, etc. But “did we send body” is not always knowable.

Ibrahim Khan: So are we converging on: default-on, but conservative; no retries for streaming; no 409; honor Retry-After; strict caps + jitter; transport-safe focus.

Rafael Mendes: Yes. And please don’t retry indefinitely on 429. Biggest incident pattern is clients auto-retrying while still over limit. If reset says 20s and they retry every 200ms, it’s pain.

Amara Diallo: Also please add a knob to disable retries entirely per request. Some customers already have a service mesh retry layer.

Dana Lo: +1. Maybe default `retries: { maxAttempts: 3 }` but allow `maxAttempts: 1` to disable. And for advanced: custom retry predicate.

Brian Murphy: We should explicitly document behavior: which status codes, how many attempts, which errors. And surface in exceptions when retries exhausted.

Ibrahim Khan: Action items:
- I’ll update the spec draft with SRE recommended defaults + “no streaming retries”.
- Rafael/Tomáš: can you sanity-check numeric defaults + the ambiguous “sent request” cases?
- Ethan/Amara: confirm which headers are guaranteed so we can write “best effort” logic.
- Dana/Mateusz: please note any language-specific limitations for “safe retry” classification.

Rafael Mendes: 👍 will review. Add an explicit note: retries must be bounded by overall timeout; no retries if it would exceed. Also add jitter requirement in bold.

Tomáš Novák: I’ll drop a short paragraph with failure modes + why aggressive defaults are risky. Useful for ADR.

Ethan Park: I’ll link the gateway header consistency PR once it’s merged. For now assume `request-id` is always present; `Retry-After` mostly for 429.

Connor O'Brien: Re: release risk: if we flip defaults to “retries on” in any SDK that was previously “off”, we need to call out as behavior change in release notes. Might be minor version but needs loud comms.

Monica Patel: Please add a mitigation note: enterprise customers can set retries off if their infra already handles it. That’ll help with security/perf reviews.

Ibrahim Khan: Great. I’ll incorporate and post updated draft in this thread later today.

Dana Lo: (reactions: :thumbsup: :eyes:)

Mateusz Zielinski: +1 (reactions: :thumbsup:)

Rafael Mendes: (reactions: :white_check_mark:)
